title: Agentic Weight-Space Programming as an Alternative to Fine-Tuning in Small Language Models
read_level: full (Zenodo record API + English PDF pre-paper.pdf of latest version 24214701 via pdftotext; Portuguese PDF not read)
metadata_mismatch: Corpus abstract empty; filled from record. PDF states 'Draft: November 13, 2026 · DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24208535'; the latest Zenodo version (record 24214701) has publication_date 2026-11-14. Title/author match.
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 agents (and Claude Fable 5.2 in two runs) read Qwen3.5-0.8B weights through the vocabulary and apply at most four rank-1 neuron-write edits, with no training, tested via a scorer with quick scores and six real test runs, to stop thinking loops.
domain: LLM math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500) with thinking loops; IFEval as second defect
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (six main runs incl. a1-a4); Claude Fable 5.2 (runs f1, f2, exploratory)
interface: code/tensor tools (rank-1 edit w_j <- w_j - alpha (u^T w_j) u on chosen output-matrix columns, |alpha| <= 10, max 4 edits)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (40 quick scores + 6 test runs of 16 practice problems)
self_editing: no; Claude agents edit a separate Qwen model
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: edits limited to "at most four rank-1 edits" on neuron groups; released a2 reduced version uses 2 edits (L16n998 and a </think> edit); per-weight counts not stated in main text

baselines_and_controls: Unedited model; Astra's published edit (reproduced); thinking off; 'Wait' word ban; budget forcing time limit; system prompt vs placebo prompt; LoRA rank-16 fine-tuning; no-agent scripted search; mean-difference edit without agent; atlas vs no-atlas agent pairs.
runs_and_variance: Six runs of winning protocol (58-67%); ten runs total on the loop defect; two locked tests of 200 (±3-4 points); exact sign tests on discordant pairs, Holm correction noted; "Rerunning the same edit with the same seeds moved it by up to 5.5 points".
robustness_of_edits: Thinking-off math and tool-calling unchanged within about two standard errors (panels detect 5-7 point changes); held-out MATH-500 tested; edits combine additively with time limit on harder math. No quantization/fine-tuning survival tests.
verification: Pre-registered dated predictions in lab notebook; second locked test with all arms fixed before opening; agent logs audited for rule violations. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Agents barred from reading Astra's edit, audited afterwards; independent agents converged on same 'Wait'-brake neurons and </think> lever; brief named the defect. Notes deleting 'Wait' neurons first backfired, and agents revised from test feedback.
limitations_stated: Small tests (200-problem locked sets, 48-148 elsewhere); thinking off is a strong cheap alternative; one model, one working defect with an easy keyword; agent may not be necessary given no-LLM searches; some first-test arms run after opening; honor-system rules audited post hoc.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, 2026)
notes_for_survey: Controlled replication of the Qwen loop-repair setting on a consumer GPU with decoding, thinking-off and LoRA baselines on pre-registered locked tests; agent edits beat LoRA and a no-agent script but exceed thinking-off by only 6.5-9 points at 2.4-3.6x its tokens. Reports proxy-score gaming and that extra interpretability context produced worse edits (3 pairs); method failed on a diffuse defect (IFEval).
